observations.body: Hebrews surveys the first tent and annual entry, then presents Christ entering the greater tent with his own blood to cleanse conscience and mediate covenant.
observations.label: Sanctuary blood is contrasted with Christ’s own blood

observations.body: The passage presents sanctuary arrangement, restricted entry, blood, conscience, covenant death, heavenly copies, and appearing as the scene's observable response or movement.

observations.body: The passage places heavenly entry beside sanctuary arrangement, restricted entry, blood, conscience, covenant death, heavenly copies, and appearing.

payload.posture: Read Hebrews 9:1–28 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the argument draws analogies and contrasts; it does not say the earthly rites never served their stated purpose
